A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bayes-error estimation work. All 36 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B.4 and D report original Bayes-error estimates, bias simulations, and corruption robustness experiments.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B.3 and D report original empirical estimates and simulations, including retained experiments and revised Figure 4 results.

M1.justification: Both versions sort corrupted soft labels, fit isotonic regression using corresponding hard labels, and average the calibrated minimum class probabilities. The new noisy-corruption theorem analyzes this existing procedure without changing its components or inputs.

E1.justification: Both use the same synthetic Gaussian and separated uniform-distribution scenarios, binarized CIFAR-10/CIFAR-10H, and Fashion-MNIST/Fashion-MNIST-H. Corruption from averaging finitely many noisy hard labels was already evaluated in v1 Appendix D.3.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain clean, hard, and corrupted estimators where applicable, histogram binning with 10/25/50/100 bins, and beta calibration alongside isotonic calibration. ViT and ResNet-18 remain the real-data reference classifiers.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix D.3 quantifies corruption using Spearman correlation; v2 Appendix D.2 drops that diagnostic and reports results against the existing hard-label counts m = 3, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100. Data generation, sample sizes, corruption parameters, and training settings otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The bias-versus-label-count analysis, corruption-parameter sweep, and noisy-corruption experiments are retained. Figure 10 contains the same estimates and confidence bands. Its new interpretation concerning small corruption derivatives does not add an empirical robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both report 95% confidence intervals from 1,000 bootstrap resamples and use 1,000 repetitions for the bias simulations. Changed confidence-interval endpoints in Figure 4 are numerical updates, without a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Under the same reported synthetic setup, Figure 4a changes estimates: isotonic approximately 7.76% to 8.01%, and clean approximately 7.50% to 7.76%. Some CIFAR-10 confidence-interval endpoints also change. Fashion-MNIST results and Figures 7, 9, and 10 retain their numerical content and principal findings.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 3 and its proof claiming an error bound depending on noise standard deviation for differentiable corruption with derivative bounded below. It removes v1 Appendix B.3's generalized Jensen theorem and associated propositions, corollaries, and examples, replacing the bias-proof foundation with Gao et al.'s result. Corollary 3 is retained in the appendix.

C1.justification: The two headline contributions concerning estimator bias and calibration-based Bayes-error estimation remain in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The introduction withdraws the subsidiary contribution claiming a newly generalized Jensen inequality of independent interest.

C2.justification: V1 identifies order-breaking corruption as theoretically unresolved. V2 presents controlled noise as covered and focuses the remaining limitation on derivatives approaching zero, explaining amplification through the inverse corruption function. Appendix D.2 reinterprets existing results around this boundary and emphasizes beta calibration's failure despite the inverse-beta corruption construction.

D1.justification: The SciPy spearmanr implementation instruction disappears with the removed correlation diagnostic. Package versions, ResNet training hyperparameters, execution times, hardware specifications, and code access remain documented; v1's separate hardware appendix is incorporated into v2 Appendix D.

R1.justification: The Jensen argument is repositioned from a new extension of Liao and Berg to an application of Gao et al., and associated references are removed. Gao's updated publication matches the work already cited in v1. The main Bayes-error positioning and Appendix A remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 relocates Corollary 3 to Appendix B.2.4, merges discussion into the conclusion, consolidates experimental and hardware details, and rewrites the robustness discussion. Citation style and author/header text change, while most retained prose and the overall narrative remain similar.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document template, title and heading typography, running headers, and reference layout throughout. Figure 4 is substantially redesigned from vertical bars arranged across two rows to three adjacent horizontal-bar panels. Figure 10 replaces the Spearman-correlation axis with hard-label count; other figures largely retain their displays.

improvement.justification: V2 streamlines the Jensen discussion and attempts to resolve v1's explicit noisy-label limitation. However, Appendix C.2 does not explain how the fourth-root concentration term arising from combining Eqs. (113)–(118) is removed in Eq. (119). This leaves the principal new theoretical benefit insufficiently established by its printed proof. With empirical coverage largely unchanged, the net quality improvement remains uncertain.
